# `ceangal.http`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py from ceangal/src/http.almd; do not edit. -->

_HTTP requests._

HTTP requests. A request returns its id at once; the answer comes to the
app's `on_result` handler (ceangal.on_result) as (id, status, body):

  var weather_req = -1
  fn refresh() -> Unit = { weather_req = http.get("https://example.com/today.json") }
  fn result(id: Int, status: Int, body: Bytes) -> Unit =
    if id == weather_req and status == 200 then weather = bytes.to_string_lossy(body) else ()
  … ceangal.app(view) |> ceangal.on_result(result)

`status` is the HTTP status, or 0 when the request failed (the body is
the error). A streamed response (server-sent events) comes in pieces
first: `is_chunk(status)`, the HTTP status being `chunk_status(status)`.
The app needs `network = true` in ceangal.toml (the Android permission,
the macOS sandbox entitlement); on the web, the server must allow the
page's origin (CORS).

```almide
import ceangal.http
```

### `request`

```almide
pub fn request(method: String, url: String, headers: List[(String, String)], body: String) -> Int
```

Start a request: method ("GET", "POST", …), URL, headers, body ("" for
none). The id it returns comes back with the answer.

### `get`

```almide
pub fn get(url: String) -> Int
```

GET `url`.

### `post_json`

```almide
pub fn post_json(url: String, body: String) -> Int
```

POST `body` as JSON.

### `cancel`

```almide
pub fn cancel(id: Int) -> Unit
```

Stop a request: nothing more arrives for it.

### `is_chunk`

```almide
pub fn is_chunk(status: Int) -> Bool
```

A piece of a streamed response (more follow, then the final status).

### `chunk_status`

```almide
pub fn chunk_status(status: Int) -> Int
```

The HTTP status of a streamed piece (the status itself otherwise).
